title: How to Hack Back Your Mind: Reclaim Control Over Your Life
author: Nir Eyal
target_audience: Adults seeking better focus and productivity
Professionals and students aiming to improve attention management
Anyone interested in building healthier digital habits
core_themes: Regaining agency over attention and time
primary_purpose: To equip readers with actionable strategies and psychological tools to reclaim control of their mind, attention, and behavior from the pervasive influence of distracting technologies, enabling them to live more intentionally and productively.

structure_format.organization: Organized into sections addressing key psychological mechanisms of distraction, practical interventions, and step-by-step habit-building exercises

key_concepts_lessons: Distraction is often an internal response to discomfort, not just a product of external triggers.
Understanding the psychological hooks of technology is essential to resisting digital manipulation.
Building ‘precommitment’ strategies and modifying environments can drastically reduce unwanted behaviors.
Time management is pain management: addressing the root cause of procrastination improves focus.
Mindfulness and self-awareness practices help intercept distractions before they take hold.
Implementing boundaries for technology use supports deeper work and more fulfilling relationships.
notable_features: Blending cognitive behavioral psychology with practical habit change techniques
Integrating up-to-date research on attention, behavior change, and technology
Step-by-step actionable frameworks for regaining focus
Customization for varying professional and personal situations
cultural_historical_context: Published in the era of ever-present digital distraction, endless notifications, and productivity challenges, the book addresses growing societal concerns about tech addiction and attention fragmentation in the 2020s.
reception_impact: Praised for translating complex behavioral science into immediately usable tactics
Recognized as a leading voice in technology mindfulness and productivity
Referenced in business, education, and mental health circles as a resource for digital well-being
Some critics note difficulty in maintaining changes without ongoing motivation and support
comparable_titles: Indistractable: How to Control Your Attention and Choose Your Life by Nir Eyal
Deep Work: Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World by Cal Newport
Digital Minimalism: Choosing a Focused Life in a Noisy World by Cal Newport
